class: Domain code built and verified only against fakes that already hold the domain's own types (Decimal money, contract keys, aware times) can be fully correct and still unusable: the first real broker reply is refused at the boundary, because nothing converts the broker's real shape (JSON numbers, SDK floats, recorder strings, a flat row with a zero average price, a symbol string instead of the contract key, naive local times) into those types.
mechanism: The parsers fail closed on any non-Decimal money and on a zero average price, and no adapter exists between the broker reply and them; tests construct domain objects directly, so the gap is invisible until a real reply is fed in.

first_seen.evidence: positions.py:53 refused average_price '5.1' and last_price '3.1' and SDK floats 5.1/3.1; positions.py:44 refused the flat row (quantity 0, average_price 0); orders/model.py:260 refused the trade price string. With 4 scaffolding adapters the same rows pass 4/4 checks (0 mismatches at entry and exit, P&L exactly -130).

fix: One broker reply adapter per endpoint (orders, trades, positions) at the app boundary: parse with parse_float=Decimal (kite_margin.py's pattern), Decimal(str(v)) for SDK floats, a flat-row rule shared with grouping.py:295, token -> contract key from the catalogue, IST attached to naive times; tested on the real recorded replies, asserting type(x) is Decimal and the exact text value.

detection.note: No adapter exists yet (GC-2b). The guard is a test that feeds the 2026-10-16 real-order recordings through the adapter into reconcile and the fill ledger and asserts 0 mismatches and P&L -130.00.

occurrences.evidence: every real orders/trades/positions row refused at the domain boundary (F-40)
